name: Garlic gel

lead: Garlic gel is a home remedy rubbed onto the scalp for alopecia areata, an autoimmune cause of patchy hair loss, with the aim of regrowing hair in bald spots.

Proponents say it stimulates the scalp and may calm local immune activity, though no mechanism has been established in the sources available. The only registered trial found was a small phase 3 study of a topical garlic concentrate in children that began in 2016 and was terminated after eight participants, with no results posted.

paras: It is discussed in non-prescription regrowth contexts and applied as a gel or preparation to patches of hair loss. It is used alongside or instead of standard alopecia areata treatments.
Raw garlic applied to skin has been reported to cause burns, and references advise caution, especially in young children. It is not an approved treatment for alopecia areata.

angle.text: Garlic gel is a folk remedy applied to bald patches in alopecia areata, with the hope of regrowth in those spots. One children's trial was registered and terminated after eight participants; raw garlic has caused skin burns.

lead: Garlic gel is a topical preparation made from garlic (Allium sativum) that has been used as a folk or alternative treatment for alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition that causes patchy hair loss. It is discussed mainly in the context of non-prescription approaches to hair regrowth rather than in appearance-optimisation forums specifically.

Only one registered clinical trial of a garlic preparation for alopecia areata appears in the registry record for this entry: a phase 3 study of a topical garlic concentrate in children that began in January 2016, enrolled eight participants and was terminated [1]. The registry entry lists no results, so no efficacy conclusion can be drawn from it.
Garlic applied raw to the skin has been reported to cause burns, and general references on garlic advise caution with topical use, particularly in young children [2].
infobox: Not an approved treatment for hair loss

paras: Garlic gel and garlic extracts are applied to the scalp by some people with patchy hair loss, in the belief that garlic stimulates regrowth. The condition they are aimed at is alopecia areata, in which the immune system attacks hair follicles.

One trial is registered: "Topical Garlic Concentrate for Alopecia Areata in Children" (NCT02691117), a phase 3 study that started on 10 January 2016 with eight participants and has the status TERMINATED [1]. No published results accompany the registration, and no other registered human studies of garlic gel for hair loss are recorded for this entry.

General references on garlic note that serious burns have resulted from raw garlic being applied topically, including for naturopathic purposes, and advise against topical use of raw garlic on young children and testing a small area first [2].

timeline.event: A phase 3 trial of topical garlic concentrate for alopecia areata in children is started (NCT02691117) and later terminated with eight participants [1].
